capital  remain available to KVI sector .  A provision for penalty should be made for  commercial banks not adhering to
the practice of providing  funds for working capital on the basis of ISEC  issued by KVIC.
(PARA 3.16.2)
 
3.17     Problems in  implementation of REGP
 
            The Committee desires that the findings of the National Level as well as  State Level Advisory Committee be
furnished to the standing Committee to the Industry on regular basis for its perusal.
 
(PARA 3.17.2)
3.18     Direction for successful implementation of REGP
 
            The Committee is of the view that despite the efforts undertaken by KVIC and the Ministry of ARI   for
successful implementation of REGP, REGP is not that much a popular programme in rural areas as its should be.  The
Commercial banks are reluctant finance under REGP and  Rural Entrepreneurs  Development  Programme  has  more or
less been a pious  programme on paper and no substantial  programme  has been taken for rehabilitation of sick units,
therefore, the Committee reiterate its observations and recommendations as made in Para 14.8
  of 124 th Report and 
further adds  that the Committee is interested in knowing the concrete the outcome of the  efforts undertaken by
Ministry of ARI in regards to strengthening of monitoring mechanism and strengthening of KVI  Boards  in order to
make KVIBs  as an instrument of  boosting rural industries.
(PARA 3.18.3)
 
3.19     NPRI’s scope
 
            The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry of ARI is taking an all out efforts to synergise efforts of all
agencies involved with cluster development for achieving rural industrialization and to prompt & promote efforts of
such agencies through financial assistance for cluster development in rural areas.   However, the Committee feels that
the Ministry of ARI  should undertake the lead role in the rural industrialization through a  holistic and co-ordinated
approach and the tangible outcome of  its  efforts  may be furnish to the Committee . 
 
(PARA 3.19.4)
3.20     Lacuna in NPRI
 
            The Committee  expect that the Ministry of ARI must go beyond  its assigned the role of a co-ordinator and
facilitator so far as the implementation of the programmes under rural industrialization is concerned.  In this regard the
Ministry of ARI must assess the actual financial requirement  for the formulation and implementation of  sustainable
programmes for rural industrialization  as only the true rural industrialization would lead to the rapid development of 

144th Report On Industry
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/144threport.htm[04-07-2016 12:45:14]
rural economy  in India.
 
(PARA 3.20.2)
 
3.21     Participation of private entrepreneur and NGO’s
 
            The Committee understands   that Institutional arrangement  is  in place for promoting  the participation  of
private entrepreneurs and NGOs, however,  till date  their participation  have remained not to the  expected  extent and
that  is why the Committee recommends that the State level implementation Committee and district level
implementation Committee should play pro-active Role in implementation of NPRI.  The Ministry of ARI should keep
on persuading the State/district level implementation  Committee for effective implementation of NPRI.
(PARA 3.21.2)
3.22     NPRI a National Mission
 
            The Committee takes note of the  steps taken by the Ministry of ARI for implementing NPRI.  However, the
steps as initiated by the Ministry of ARI  is paltry keeping in view the length and breadth of rural India, therefore, the
Committee reiterates its recommendations as made in Para 15.12 of 124
th Report. 
(PARA 3.22.2)
 
3.23     Recovery of loan from State KVI Boards
 
            The Committee appreciates the endorsement of the recommendation of this Committee for the need for chalking
out  Action Plan for  recovery of loans from KVI boards , however, the Committee feels that  success of so  envisaged
plan depends upon the facts that no substantial KVIC  remained outstanding with KVI Boards.  Recycling and
circulation of working capital would keep the industry running.
(PARA 3.23.2)
RECOMMENDATION
 
3.24     Benefits of North-Eastern Region and Sikkim
 
            The Committee  expects that KVIC would furnish in its action taken note of the present report the details of
appropriation of    10% capital expenditure  earmarked under major head  4552 and the steps taken  for the proper
utilization alongwith the actual achievement during the year 2003-04.
(PARA 3.24.2)
3.25     Implementing the employment programmes
 
            It is on the basis of information furnished by the Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries the Committee,
recommended that  in order to bring uniformity in approach and implementation of employment generation
programmes, all schemes should be integrated and co-ordinated under one Ministry and uniformity should be brought in
the mode of implementation of schemes.  The Committee while recommending for bringing all the schemes under one
Ministry does not intend to dilute the modalities and target groups of the employment generation programme.  Rather
the  Committee intends that with the administration of all the employment generation programmes under one Ministry
will give the “focused–attention” of the Government to combat the twin problem of unemployment and poverty.  The
Committee, therefore, reiterates its view point and recommendation.
(PARA 3.25.2)
GENERAL ISSUES
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
3.26     Synergistic approach towards implementation of rural infrastructural development
 
            The Committee understands that the soul of India dwells in village area and in order to transform the status of
Indian economy from developing to a developed one, a very serious effort is required to overhaul the rural economy by

144th Report On Industry
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/144threport.htm[04-07-2016 12:45:14]
undertaking  programmes for rural industrialization and development.  It is here at the “Unified and Integrated Planning
System and holistic approach” to strike out the very roots of poverty and  to  undertake the implementation of well
knitted policies/programmes is required for the purpose.   The Committee knows that the Allocation of Business well
defines the jurisdiction of the Ministries/Departments of Government.   However, strict  adherence to the principle of
water tight compartmentalization would not help in the smooth transaction of the business of the Government.  An
integrated and co-ordinated planning and approach is required.  It is under this vision the Committee recommended that
the Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries may be either integrated and merged with Ministry of Rural Development,
Ministry of Poverty Alleviation, Food Processing or a Committee of Secretaries headed by Senior most Secretary of
these Ministries be constituted for better coordination and result oriented approach.
 
(PARA 3.26.2)
3.27     Survey of sick units and chalk out rehabilitations programmes
 
            The Committee feels that the basic question arises  whether any survey of  sick units have been under taken by
the Ministry of ARI or not and what action plan  have been chalked out/implemented for rehabilitation of these sick
units, the Committee  is interested to know.
(PARA 3.27.2)
 
3.28     Creating gainful employment on the sustainable basis
 
 
            The Committee feels that the Ministry of  ARI in its action taken note should have furnished  the steps taken by
the Ministry in regard to the  integration of  India’s Agro and Rural Industries with the global economy under the WTO
regime.
 
(PARA 3.28.2)
 
3.29     National Policy for Agro and Rural Industries
 
 
            The Committee is pleased to note that KVIC  had organized the National  Convention on Rural Industrialization
at New Delhi in march, 2003 and the Gramodaya  Manthan at Wardha in September , 2003 to seek the opinion of all 
stakeholders in the rural industrialization process .  The  outcome of these activities/efforts on the process of formulation
of National Policy for Agro and Rural Industries ( encompassing  the  ingredients  as detailed in Para  20.6.2 of the
Committee’s 124
th Report ) may be furnished to the Committee in line with the true sprit of the recommendations of the
Committee.
 
(PARA 3.29.2)
 
3.30     Institutional credit flow to ARI Sector
           
            The Committee would like to be apprised  of the status of institutional credit flow  to Agro and Rural industries ,
sector-wise and the extent of participation of RRBs in the implementation of REGP .  The requisite information may be
furnished to the Committee in the action taken  note of the present report.
(PARA 3.30.2)
 
3.31     Disguised unemployment in ARI     
 
            Action is required on the part of Ministry of ARI in line with the recommendation of the Committee. 
 
(PARA 3.31.2)
3.32     Merger of all Government’s schemes for employment generation into one programme
